anomalies.description: Sudden massive explosion at 6.0s: intense white-orange flash fills the frame, consistent with instantaneous blast, debris and fireball expanding outward—matches expected anomaly type of explosion.

original_descriptions.description: Sudden massive explosion at 6.0s: intense white-orange flash fills the frame, consistent with instantaneous blast, debris and fireball expanding outward—matches expected anomaly type of explosion.

Sudden massive explosion at 0.03s (frame 3), characterized by an intense bright flash, instantaneous outward ejection of debris, and rapid formation of a dense smoke/dust cloud engulfing the gas station area; structural elements (e.g., corrugated metal sheets) are violently displaced and scattered, consistent with a high-energy blast event.

Sudden large smoke/dust cloud appears instantaneously with scattered corrugated metal debris on the ground, consistent with an explosion; frames 0–10 show aftermath (smoke, debris, distortion), while frame 11 shows the scene pre-event (clear, intact), indicating a sudden blast occurred between frames 10 and 11.

Sudden violent explosion at a fuel station: bright flash (frame 4), followed by rapid debris ejection, structural collapse of corrugated metal panels, and immediate dense smoke/dust cloud (frames 5–12), consistent with an instantaneous blast event.

Sudden violent disruption with large corrugated metal sheets violently displaced outward, thick smoke/dust cloud rapidly expanding from a central point, and debris scattered across the ground—consistent with an explosion occurring between frames 1 and 2 (18.0s–18.5s). No visible fire or human actors, but the instantaneous structural failure and blast dynamics meet the expected anomaly signature for an explosion.

Scene shows aftermath of a sudden explosion: large smoke/dust cloud filling the area, corrugated metal sheets violently displaced and scattered, debris on ground, and structural damage visible. No visible flash in these frames, but the instantaneous dispersion of debris and dense smoke cloud is consistent with an explosion occurring just prior to or at the start of this segment (22.5s–26.1s).
